attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the conditional argument in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the same-system chess antecedent and restriction to learning from statistical data alone. The categorical wording commits to a conditional negative prediction without a deadline.

contract.note: The operational readings of robust chess knowledge and reliable everyday reasoning are reasonable. Marcus supplies neither numerical thresholds nor a precise training boundary, so what qualifies as a decisive counterexample depends on these supplied interpretations.

evidence.note: Timely experiments establish repeated chess-rule failures in evaluated systems. This supports the antecedent only; it does not establish the predicted broader limitation.
Demonstrates substantial learned chess competence and limits generalisations about statistical models. It does not show broad everyday competence in a system meeting the antecedent.
The dated temporal benchmark is relevant background, but supplies no matched chess evaluation or demonstration across all named domains.
Financial reasoning results document capabilities and limitations, but do not establish the required same-system combination or a necessary connection to chess-rule failures.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes the chess limitation for some evaluated systems but neither a necessary barrier to broader competence nor a qualifying counterexample. Learned chess competence was considered but does not contradict this conditional. No deadline or conclusive event permits resolution.
